description: EXPERIMENTAL. Step 2 of 2: publish the signed agent manifest to the site, using the `manifestId` from build_agent_manifest and the signature the user produced over its `signingInput`. `signature` must be the 64-byte r||s pair base64url-encoded — NOT the DER/ASN.1 blob `openssl dgst -sign` writes, which has to be converted first. If the user hands you DER output, say so rather than sending it. Porkbun verifies the signature exactly as an outside party would BEFORE writing anything: if it does not verify, nothing is published and the failing check is named (APM_SIGNATURE_INVALID). The artifacts are re-hashed too, so if the site changed since the manifest was built you get APM_ARTIFACTS_CHANGED and should build again. On success the manifest is written to /.well-known/apm.json and the response includes `manifestSha256` and a `verifyUrl` anyone can check with no API key. SERVING CAN LAG THE WRITE by up to a couple of minutes, so if you verify immediately and the response's manifestSha256 does not match the one you just published, you are reading the previous file - wait and check again rather than reporting a failure. The manifest_id is single-use once a publish succeeds (a failed one can be retried); re-using a spent one returns APM_MANIFEST_ALREADY_PUBLISHED, which is not the same as APM_MANIFEST_EXPIRED. Tell the user they must re-publish whenever a listed file changes, because the manifest records hashes and an edited file stops matching until they do. Use dry_run to confirm the signature is good without writing.

domain.description: Fully qualified domain name in the account, e.g. `example.com`

dry_run.description: Verify and report what would be published, without writing.

manifest_id.description: From build_agent_manifest. Guarantees the bytes verified are the bytes signed.

signature.description: ES256 signature over signingInput: 64-byte r||s, base64url.
